newsitem.title: USA: Bank of New York to buy Wells Fargo custody business.
newsitem.headline: Bank of New York to buy Wells Fargo custody business.

text.p: Bank of New York Co. Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy the institutional custody and Taft-Hartley custody businesses of Wells Fargo and Co.
Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Bank of New York said the deal is expected to add about $75 billion to its assets under custody, which now total more than $3 trillion.

Bank of New York said client services will be provided through its BNY Western Trust Company's West Coast offices. BNY Western Trust provides custody and corporate trust services in 12 Western states.
"This is a strategic market for us and we look forward to providing these new clients with a superior level of service," Thomas Renyi, president of Bank of New York Co. Inc., said in a statement.
Wells Fargo Vice Chairman Clyde Ostler said the agreement will allow Wells Fargo to focus more resources on its employee benefit trust and investment management businesses.
A spokeswoman for Bank of New York said the transaction was expected to close in the second half of the year.

In an interview on May 13 at Bank of New York's annual meeting, Chairman J. Carter Bacot said the bank holding company would continue seeking acquisitions in securities processing and custody. He said the businesses had good profit margins and were attractive acquisitions amid a wave of consolidation.

Bank of New York's custody clients include insurance companies, central banks, commercial banks and government agencies. Custody accounts for labour unions comprise the Taft-Hartley business Bank of New York is buying.
